questions._flag: OFFICIAL KEY GIVES TWO ANSWERS: the marking scheme prints 'Ans: (B) -2 OR (C) -3/2'. Recorded as B, the first CBSE lists. Cause, checked against the printed page (the 1/3 is on the question paper AND in the marking scheme's own reproduction): with that 1/3 scaling AB = I is UNSATISFIABLE for any lambda - the (1,1) entry is (1/3)(-2-9+12) = 1/3, not 1. The un-scaled matrix IS exactly A-inverse (det A = -1, adj A = [[2,0,-1],[-9,-2,3],[-6,-1,2]]), which gives lambda = -2; equating only the (3,3) entry of the printed product to 1 gives (9+4L)/3 = 1, i.e. lambda = -3/2. Rows 1 and 2 of column 3 both give -2, row 3 gives -3/2 - hence the double key. Transcribed as printed, 1/3 included.
